title: Discuss missed commitments
context: Asha missed 3 of 8 client reports in September. Ravi needs a dependable Friday handoff.
question: Explain the observed pattern and impact. Ask Asha what got in the way; agree one measurable next step.
independentQuestion: Asha disputes a missed date and shares a dependency log. Revise the facts and agree a fair checkpoint.

title: Recognise results without overlooking behaviour
context: Nikhil exceeded sales target by 12%, but 2 colleagues report unannounced handoff changes.
question: Recognise the result, name the handoff behaviour and impact, and invite Nikhil to agree a practical change.
independentQuestion: Nikhil asks whether results no longer matter. Explain how outcomes and collaboration both inform the review.

title: Open a performance improvement conversation
context: Meera has 4 overdue reconciliations. Her manager Dev must explain a documented 30-day support plan.
question: Describe the verified gap, expectations and support. Check understanding; do not predict employment outcomes.
independentQuestion: Meera reports missing system access. Adjust the support plan and agree who will restore access by Monday.

title: Review a support-plan checkpoint
context: At day 14, Arjun met 2 of 3 agreed checks. One client response is still unverified.
question: Separate confirmed progress from the missing evidence. Agree the next check and an explicit owner.
independentQuestion: The client confirms they caused the delay. Update the assessment and explain the remaining expectation.

title: Explain a compensation constraint
context: Leena requests a 15% increase. Omar can confirm a 6% team budget, not individual outcomes.
question: Explain what is known and what you cannot promise. Acknowledge the concern and name the review process.
independentQuestion: Leena brings a written external offer. Clarify the decision route without promising a matching counter-offer.

title: Respond to a pay-equity concern
context: Priya believes a peer earns ₹80,000 more. HR partner Kunal cannot share another person's salary.
question: Acknowledge the concern, protect confidentiality and explain the evidence and review channel available to Priya.
independentQuestion: Priya asks for the peer's payslip. Decline respectfully and offer a review of her own role and pay factors.

title: Explain a promotion decision
context: Sana was not promoted after 2 strong projects. Evidence of cross-team ownership is incomplete.
question: State the decision clearly, explain the evidence gap and agree specific opportunities without promising promotion.
independentQuestion: Sana presents a cross-team project you missed. Explain how the new evidence can be reviewed and by whom.

title: Reset an implied promotion promise
context: Vikram understood 'next cycle' as a promise. Manager Tara has no approved opening in the 6-person team.
question: Own the ambiguity, separate aspiration from an approved commitment and agree a documented development conversation.
independentQuestion: A vacancy opens in another team. Explain the application route without implying a guaranteed outcome.

title: Listen to a resignation
context: Isha resigns with 30 days' notice after 2 years. Mohan needs a handover but should not pressure her.
question: Acknowledge Isha's decision, ask what she is willing to share and agree an initial handover discussion.
independentQuestion: Isha declines to discuss her reasons. Respect that boundary and confirm only the practical transition needs.

title: Discuss a possible counter-offer
context: Rahul asks for a 20% counter-offer by Friday. Neha can seek approval but cannot commit funds.
question: Clarify Rahul's priorities and your authority. Explain the approval route and the time you will next update him.
independentQuestion: Approval covers 10%, not 20%. State the limit directly and allow Rahul to decide without guilt or pressure.

title: Receive an employee complaint
context: Ananya says a supervisor interrupted her in 3 meetings. HR partner Farah has not checked the events.
question: Listen without deciding the allegation. Explain next steps, confidentiality limits and the immediate support options.
independentQuestion: Ananya asks for guaranteed secrecy. Explain who may need information and ask about her concerns.

title: Give a complaint-process update
context: Kabir raised a concern 10 days ago. Two interviews are complete and one witness is unavailable.
question: Explain the process status without sharing witness details or implying a finding. Set a realistic next update.
independentQuestion: Kabir asks whether silence means failure. Explain what remains unresolved and the escalation channel.

title: Announce a team restructure
context: A 12-person support team will become 2 groups next month. Reporting lines are confirmed; shifts are not.
question: Explain the reason, what changes now and what is still undecided. Give a named contact and next update date.
independentQuestion: A colleague asks if roles will be cut. Use only confirmed decisions and explain how updates will be shared.

title: Discuss a changed reporting line
context: Jaya will report to Amit from 1 November. Her role scope is unchanged, but a client handoff is unresolved.
question: Explain the confirmed change and its practical impact. Ask for concerns and agree the first transition action.
independentQuestion: Jaya identifies a client approval risk. Adjust the handoff plan and assign an owner to confirm the approval.

title: Raise a skip-level capacity concern
context: A 5-person team has 11 urgent requests. Team lead Rohan has not responded to 2 capacity reviews.
question: Present the verified workload and prior attempts neutrally. Ask the skip-level leader for a prioritisation decision.
independentQuestion: The leader says all requests remain urgent. Propose trade-offs and ask who will own the remaining risk.

title: Respond to an unexpected skip-level escalation
context: Elena learns that Sam escalated a delivery concern to her director yesterday; the client date is 48 hours away.
question: Discuss the delivery facts without retaliation. Ask what prevented an earlier conversation and agree an escalation route.
independentQuestion: Sam shows a message Elena missed. Own the gap and agree how urgent concerns will be confirmed next time.

title: Give feedback to a senior peer
context: Director Vivek changed the scope twice after sign-off. Naina's team spent 16 hours reworking the proposal.
question: Describe the observable changes and cost respectfully. Invite Vivek's context and propose a scope-change checkpoint.
independentQuestion: Vivek names a new regulatory dependency. Adapt the checkpoint to urgent exceptions and keep decisions visible.

title: Address interruptions by a senior peer
context: In 2 planning meetings, Arun cut off Pooja before the risk summary. The team approved a ₹4 lakh pilot.
question: Raise the specific pattern privately, explain its decision impact and ask for a way to protect risk discussion.
independentQuestion: Arun says time was limited. Propose a brief risk slot and a signal to continue the discussion separately.

title: Recommend a hiring priority
context: Suresh has budget for 1 hire, while operations requests 2 and finance requests 1 for month-end coverage.
question: Compare demand, risk and timing using known facts. Recommend a first hire and a review point for the other requests.
independentQuestion: Operations fills a vacancy internally. Reassess your recommendation and explain what evidence changed it.

title: Resolve conflicting availability expectations
context: A 7-person team spans Pune and London. Aditi received 4 late-night requests last week without agreed urgency rules.
question: Explain the impact, ask about genuine urgent needs and propose a clear availability and escalation agreement.
independentQuestion: An incident occurs outside agreed hours. Apply an exception path and adjust the next day's workload.
